hints: Think about what happens to the C=C double bond when an alkene polymerises, and what is left in the polymer chain.
Statement 1 is true because a saturated poly(alkene) has no pi bond to attack bromine in the dark.
Check the other two ideas about burning plastics and burying them in landfill, then pick the combination that includes every true statement.
walkthrough:
**What is a poly(alkene) really?**

Think of poly(ethene) made from ethene. The pi bond opens up to join monomers together.

$$n\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{-[CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-]_n$$
The product has only single C-C and C-H bonds, it is saturated.

**Check statement 1: reaction with bromine**

Alkenes decolourise $\text{Br}_2(aq)$ by electrophilic addition across C=C. Poly(alkenes) have no C=C left.
So they do not react with $\text{Br}_2(aq)$ in the dark. Statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2: combustion for disposal**

Poly(alkenes) are hydrocarbons. Complete combustion gives $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, but incomplete combustion gives toxic $\text{CO}$ and soot.
Chlorinated polymers like PVC also give $\text{HCl}$. So harmful products are possible. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3: biodegradability**

The C-C backbone is non-polar, strong and unreactive to enzymes and water. Microorganisms cannot easily break it down.
That is why plastic waste persists in landfill. Statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the conclusions**

All three statements, 1, 2 and 3, are correct. Choose the option that includes 1, 2 and 3.

options.A: Correct. All three are true. No C=C remains for bromine addition, combustion can give CO, soot or HCl, and the inert saturated chain resists biodegradation.
options.B: Incorrect. This omits statement 3. Students sometimes think all carbon-based polymers biodegrade, but the non-polar C-C chain of poly(alkenes) is very resistant to microbial attack.
options.C: Incorrect. This omits statement 1. Students sometimes think the polymer still contains alkenes because of its name, but polymerisation consumes the double bonds so no reaction with Br2(aq) occurs.
options.D: Incorrect. This includes only statement 1. It wrongly rejects the environmental issues. Both incomplete combustion hazards and lack of biodegradability are key properties of poly(alkenes).
